narrative.overview: The site is a working index, not a promotional shell. It presents a maker's real software on a cool neutral surface, then uses product-specific color only where it identifies a project. A compact studio rail establishes authorship; the project index does the actual work. The visual system deliberately replaces the previous warm-paper editorial mood. It also avoids the generic SaaS hero: no repeated eyebrow labels, no equal feature-card wall as the page structure, and no single desktop-window metaphor imposed on every future project.
keyCharacteristics: Cool neutral ground with a saturated electric-blue brand signal.
Real project interfaces are the primary imagery and evidence.
Product type controls the preview shell; the global shell stays platform-neutral.
One-pixel rules, restrained radii, and dense but scannable metadata.
Light and dark themes use the same hierarchy and spacing.

rules.name: The One Lab Blue Rule
rules.body: The global brand blue is rare. It appears in navigation actions, focus, selection, and brand signals, not as decoration on every section.

rules.name: The Product Owns Its Accent Rule
rules.body: Violet, teal, blue, and orange identify projects. They may color a preview bar, a project link, and small data markers; they do not recolor the global navigation or whole page bands.

rules.name: The No Decorative Eyebrow Rule
rules.body: Headings carry their own hierarchy. Do not place a tracked uppercase kicker above a section heading.

rules.name: The Zero Tracking Rule
rules.body: Chinese headings and body copy keep letter-spacing: 0; hierarchy comes from size and weight rather than cramped negative tracking.

rules.name: The Artifact Depth Rule
rules.body: A screenshot may feel like a physical working window. Page sections do not float as cards and cards are never nested.

dos: Do lead with real interfaces and working artifacts.
Do keep the global shell neutral and let project type or per-project tone own the preview.
Do use 6px-8px radii, one-pixel rules, and 44px interactive targets.
Do preserve WCAG AA body-text contrast in both themes.
Do let future projects map to desktop, browser, phone, code, or image preview shells.
donts: Don't restore the warm cream paper ground, tiny tracked mono eyebrows, or decorative editorial hairlines.
Don't force every project into a desktop window.
Don't turn the index into equal marketing cards with icon-plus-heading-plus-copy.
Don't use product accents on page-wide background bands.
Don't nest cards or use colored side borders as decoration.
